name: LF355 / LF356 / LF357 (LF155 / LF156 / LF157)
tagline: National's 1975 BI-FET original, the first monolithic JFET-input op-amp: 12 nV/√Hz, 12 V/µs. TI still makes the LF356.

lineage.note: LF156 launched 1975 as 'the first monolithic JFET input operational amplifier'. Price fell from $2 to 75 cents by 1978.
Second-sourced 'a better-performing LF356'; its OP-15/16/17 were 'patterned after the 355/356/357' (Jung).
1990s Motorola PSpice library (MOTOR.LIB) contains an 'LF356M' model.
Own 'Wide bandwidth single J-FET operational amplifiers' datasheet; reportedly still made after National stopped (Tangent).
Unverified; only evidence is Tangent's remark in a Chinese translation.
Reissued as SNOSBH0 (Rev D 2015). Folders LF156, LF256, LF356, LF356-MIL. FFAB BI-FET qualified 2018.

reputation.summary: Historically important more than currently praised. Walt Jung's 1978 survey called the 355/356/357 'second-generation FET' op-amps with better drift and offset. National stressed low noise, fast settling and capacitive-load stability. Tangent likens the LF355 to the TL071 and finds it unsuitable for low-impedance headphones. It survives in synth, sample-and-hold, I/V and lab circuits.
typical_uses: DAC I/V converters and fast D/A or A/D buffers
High-impedance buffers, photodiode and electrometer front ends
Active filters and vintage synth VCO/VCF circuits
caveats: Input past the negative CM limit (−12 V typ, −10 V guaranteed) reverses phase; below V− can destroy it.
Reversed insertion or supply can fuse internal conductors, a real risk when rolling.
LF357/LF157/LF257 is decompensated (AV≥5) and oscillates as a follower; not a drop-in for LF356.
5 mA typ draw for a FET single; self-heating raises bias. Poor at driving low impedances.
Single pinout; offset pot wiper to V+ on pins 1/5. 1975 LF156 needs pin 8 tied to 7.

counterfeit_notes: No documented fakes. Main risk: remarked LF351/TL081-class parts. Genuine LF356 draws about 5 mA (LF351 about 1.8 mA) and has about 5 MHz GBW. TI marks 'LF 356N' or 'LF356 M'. Distrust post-2012 'National' date codes and unity-gain-stable 'LF357H'.

silicon_changes.summary: TI PCN 20180920003.1 moves select BiFET devices from Greenock GFAB6 (150 mm, closing) to FFAB BiFET 200 mm; qualification approved 19 Sep 2018, first ship 25 Dec 2018. LF356 wafer, can, SOIC and PDIP listed. Mask change not stated.
silicon_changes.identification: Not visible in the marking; SNOSBH0D unchanged. Only TI lot trace or date codes after Dec 2018 would indicate FFAB wafers.

spec_deltas.before: GFAB6 BiFET 150 mm, Greenock (earlier: previous (National-heritage) fab, not named in the retrieved document)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented; datasheet limits unchanged and no pre- versus post-transfer measurements known.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same datasheet, pinout and limits; no published parametric change.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN title, dates, GFAB6-to-FFAB move confirmed; LF356 row garbled in one extract.

silicon_changes.summary: The 1975 LF156 pinout made pin 8 a bias reference, with typical 15 V/µs and 1.4 µs versus 12 V/µs and 1.5 µs from 1980. Possibly an early mask or metal change; bonding-only change or preliminary specs would also explain it.
silicon_changes.identification: 1975 sheet labels pin 8 'current source reference', tie to pin 7 if offset unused; 1980 on shows NC. Metal-can LF156s, c. 1975–76 date codes.

spec_deltas.before: Current source reference; tie to pin 7 if offset adjust unused

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None known; matters only for very early metal-can LF156s with pin 8 left open.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: only rare 1975-era LF156 cans; tie pin 8 to V+ when not trimming.
silicon_changes.verification: Based on the 1975 advance sheet versus the 1980 datasheet; die change is an inference.

silicon_changes.summary: The LF157/LF357 schematic note changed from 2 pF to 3 pF and the feature-list load claim from 10,000 pF to 5,000 pF (the hint still says 0.01 µF). Could be a compensation change or a documentation fix. GBW (20 MHz) and slew (50 V/µs) unchanged.
silicon_changes.identification: 'C = 2 pF on LF157' (1980) versus '*C = 3pF in LF357 series' (2000/2001 and TI Rev D). No date code or PCN boundary known.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: guaranteed specs identical; change may be purely editorial.
silicon_changes.verification: Later 3 pF note confirmed in a National copy; 1980 '2 pF' wording not found online.

silicon_changes.summary: Second-source dies were not necessarily National's. Electronics (June 1978) says PMI offered 'a better-performing LF356'; LT's 1990 models claim 'Low IOS 10pA max'. ST's own datasheet (date unknown) was not examined.
silicon_changes.identification: Manufacturer logo: PMI, LT or ST/SGS versus NS or TI.

spec_deltas.after: LT second source: 10 pA (per macromodel header)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Negligible for audio; known differences are in DC precision.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same pinout and function; specs may differ by vendor.
silicon_changes.verification: Second-source differences not checked further; an ST LF357 datasheet is confirmed to exist.

PCN 20180920003.1 'FFAB BIFET Technology Qualification', approved 19-Sep-2018, lists LF356 MWC, H, M, N (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/2674716.pdf).
LF356-MIL Active, SOIC-8/TO-CAN-8, 36 V, 5 MHz, 12 V/µs, 'first monolithic JFET-input op amp' (https://www.ti.com/product/LF356-MIL).
